skill.name: image-inpainting
skill.description: Mask-driven local image editing through RunComfy inpainting models, with fallback guidance for description-based edits when a mask is unavailable.
skill.summary: Use RunComfy to fill or replace masked image regions while preserving surrounding content.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, documentation links, or model-selection text rather than executable code. I found no prompt injection evidence. The skill sends user image and mask URLs to RunComfy and promotes watermark removal, so authorization boundaries are needed.

remediation.suggestion: Disclose that images and masks are processed by RunComfy. Ask for confirmation before sending private or regulated content.
Limit examples to user-owned or licensed assets. Remove generic watermark-removal phrasing or add authorization checks.
Keep automated Bash usage limited to runcomfy commands. Do not add package-manager install commands to agent workflows.
Do not ask agents to read the token file. Use runcomfy login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for authentication.

content.value_statement: Precise local image edits are hard when only one region should change. This skill routes masked images through RunComfy inpainting models and suggests fallback edit models when no mask exists.
actual_capabilities: Selects Z-Image Turbo Inpainting when image and mask URLs are available.
Explains prompt, image, mask, strength, control scale, and seed options.
Provides RunComfy CLI examples for object removal and region replacement.
Recommends description-based edit models when no mask exists.
Documents exit codes and retryable RunComfy failures.
limitations: It does not create masks. A mask URL must come from another tool.
It requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy login or token.
Image and mask URLs are processed by external RunComfy endpoints.
It does not cover outpainting or frame-by-frame video inpainting.

use_cases.title: Retouch Product Photos
use_cases.description: Replace a masked background while keeping the product, shadows, and edges consistent.

use_cases.title: Clean Local Image Defects
use_cases.description: Fill a masked scratch, blemish, or damaged area without changing the rest of the image.

use_cases.title: Choose the Correct Edit Route
use_cases.description: Decide whether a masked inpainting model or description-based edit model fits the request.

prompt_templates.title: Remove Object with Mask
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image-inpainting skill to remove the object covered by my mask. Preserve lighting, texture, and all unmasked areas.

prompt_templates.title: Replace Masked Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Z-Image Turbo Inpainting for this image and mask. Replace only the masked background with a light gray studio backdrop.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Inpainting Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a RunComfy inpainting request for this image, mask, and edit goal. Recommend strength, control scale, and preservation language first.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Complex Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the mask-driven and description-based routes for this edit. Select the model, explain why, then run the chosen RunComfy workflow.

output_examples.input: A masked product photo has a cluttered shelf behind the subject.
output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo Inpainting because a mask exists.
It recommends a high strength setting for a full background replacement.
The result should preserve the product edges and replace only the masked shelf.

output_examples.input: A portrait has a small masked blemish on one cheek.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends low strength cleanup and preservation language for skin tone, texture, lighting, and nearby facial features.

output_examples.input: The user has no mask and asks to remove a described object.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a description-based edit model and asks for spatial details before running the edit.

best_practices: Use image and mask URLs that the user explicitly provided for this edit.
Soften mask edges slightly and describe what must stay unchanged.
Start with lower strength for cleanup and increase only for full replacement.
anti_patterns: Running edits on images the user did not provide or authorize.
Using a broad mask when only a small region should change.
Treating description-based fallback as pixel-precise when a mask is required.

faq.question: Does this skill create the mask for me?
faq.answer: No. It expects an image URL and a mask URL from another tool.

faq.question: Which model does it use first?
faq.answer: It uses Z-Image Turbo Inpainting when a mask is available.

faq.question: What happens if I do not have a mask?
faq.answer: It recommends a description-based edit model that can target a region from text.

faq.question: Can it preserve everything outside the mask?
faq.answer: Yes, that is the intended workflow. Clear preservation instructions improve the result.

faq.question: Does it upload images to a third-party service?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI sends the request to RunComfy processing endpoints.

faq.question: Can I use it for copyrighted or watermarked images?
faq.answer: Use it only on images you own, license, or have clear permission to edit.
